questions.q: What does Yahweh tell Jeremiah to do with the linen loincloth?
questions.a: He tells Jeremiah to put the loincloth on and then take it to Perath and hide it there.

questions.q: Where did Jeremiah hide the loincloth?
questions.a: He hid it by Perath, just as Yahweh had commanded him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to do after many days had passed?
questions.a: He told Jeremiah to go to Perath and get the loincloth that he had hidden there.

questions.q: What was the quality of the loincloth when Jeremiah dug it out from where he had hidden it?
questions.a: It was ruined and no good for anything.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: He says he will ruin the great pride of Judah and Jerusalem.

questions.q: How are the wicked people like the loincloth?
questions.a: They are good for nothing because they refuse to listen to Yahweh’s word.

questions.q: What three things does Yahweh want his people to do?
questions.a: He wants them to honor him, praise him, and glorify him.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell Jeremiah to say to the people about the jars?
questions.a: He tells him to say that every jar will be filled with wine.

questions.q: What will Yahweh fill all the people with?
questions.a: He will fill them with drunkenness.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do after he fills the people with drunkenness?
questions.a: He will destroy them.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the people to do instead of being proud?
questions.a: He tells them to listen carefully because Yahweh has spoken.

questions.q: What will happen if the people do not give honor to Yahweh?
questions.a: He will bring darkness.

questions.q: What will Jeremiah do if the people do not listen?
questions.a: He will cry secretly because of their pride, since Yahweh’s people will be taken captive.

questions.q: Why should the king and queen mother humble themselves?
questions.a: Their enemies will soon take their glorious crowns from their heads.

questions.q: What will happen to all of Judah?
questions.a: All of Judah will be taken captive.

questions.q: What does Yahweh tell the leaders of Jerusalem to look at?
questions.a: He tells them to look at the enemies coming from the north.

questions.q: Whom will Yahweh place over the people?
questions.a: He will place over them those whom they had taught to be their friends.

questions.q: Why are bad things happening to the people?
questions.a: Bad things are happening because the people have committed many iniquities.

questions.q: What does Yahweh compare the people’s inability to change to?
questions.a: He compares it to a Cushite trying to change his skin or a leopard trying to change its spots.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do to the people?
questions.a: He will scatter them like stubble in the wind.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say the people have done that leads to their punishment?
questions.a: They have forgotten Yahweh and trusted in a lie.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to expose the people’s shame?
questions.a: He will strip off their skirts over their faces so that their shame will be visible to everyone.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say about the evil things the people have done in secret?
questions.a: He says that he has seen their evil deeds, and that Jerusalem has remained unclean for a long time.

commentary.text: The glory of the Jews should be marred. (Jer. 13:1-11) All ranks should suffer misery, An earnest exhortation to repentance. (Jer. 13:12-17) An awful message to Jerusalem and its king. (Jer. 13:18-27)

Jer. 13:1-11 It was usual with the prophets to teach by signs. And we have the explanation, Jer. 13:9-11. The people of Israel had been to God as this girdle. He caused them to cleave to him by the law he gave them, the prophets he sent among them, and the favours he showed them. They had by their idolatries and sins buried themselves in foreign earth, mingled among the nations, and were so corrupted that they were good for nothing. If we are proud of learning, power, and outward privileges, it is just with God to wither them. The minds of men should be awakened to a sense of their guilt and danger; yet nothing will be effectual without the influences of the Spirit.

Jer. 13:12-17 As the bottle was fitted to hold the wine, so the sins of the people made them vessels of wrath, fitted for the judgments of God; with which they should be filled till they caused each other's destruction. The prophet exhorts them to give glory to God, by confessing their sins, humbling themselves in repentance, and returning to his service. Otherwise they would be carried into other countries in all the darkness of idolatry and wickedness. All misery, witnessed or foreseen, will affect a feeling mind, but the pious heart must mourn most over the afflictions of the Lord's flock.

Jer. 13:18-27 Here is a message sent to king Jehoiakim, and his queen. Their sorrows would be great indeed. Do they ask, Wherefore come these things upon us? Let them know, it is for their obstinacy in sin. We cannot alter the natural colour of the skin; and so is it morally impossible to reclaim and reform these people. Sin is the blackness of the soul; it is the discolouring of it; we were shapen in it, so that we cannot get clear of it by any power of our own. But Almighty grace is able to change the Ethiopian's skin. Neither natural depravity, nor strong habits of sin, form an obstacle to the working of God, the new-creating Spirit. The Lord asks of Jerusalem, whether she is determined not be made clean. If any poor slave of sin feels that he could as soon change his nature as master his headstrong lusts, let him not despair; for things impossible to men are possible with God. Let us then seek help from Him who is mighty to save.
